title: Document/support process for using custom mavlink dialect
author: Ryanf55
body:
I want to add a few custom mavlink messages for my own dialect, not part of upstream, and develop without having to commit and push to a repository.

Right now, mavlink is brought in through ExternalProject_add like so:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L32-L45



The URL is hard-coded to upstream
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L34

Then, for a local build, mavlink is built and installed, so that its config file is on disk.
This allows it to be found through find_package:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L4

For some reason, regardless of the setting for the MAVLINK_DIALECT, it does not get affect the command here:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L27-L39


I want to

* Add a new local mavlink XML dialect, say my_custom.xml
* Get MAVSDK to also generate that dialect in addition to the normal dialect
* Use those new messages to send custom packets via mavsdk

Can we either document or add support for mavlink to be brought in through a submodule, fetchcontent, or how to build/install mavlink on the system that does not rely on merging stuff upstream first? Perhaps we can support a way where mavlink on the system can be used.

In mavlink:
```
cmake -B build -DMAVLINK_DIALECT=MyCustomDialect
cmake --build build
cmake --install build --prefix install
```
Which generates the following header (as expected)
```
/home/ryan/Dev/mavlink/install/include/mavlink/MyCustomDialect/mavlink_msg_my_custom_dialect_toy.h
```
Then, when building MAVSDK, perhaps we can allow a user to add "/path/to/mavlink/install" to the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH and use that version instead of pulling from upstream.

Trying this today results in the following error:
```
gmake[2]: *** No rule to make target 'third_party/install/include/mavlink/message_definitions/v1.0/ardupilotmega.xml', needed by 'src/mavsdk/core/embedded_mavlink_xml.h'.  Stop.
gmake[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/Makefile2:910: src/mavsdk/core/CMakeFiles/generate_core_mavlink_xml_header.dir/all] Error 2
gmake: *** [Makefile:136: all] Error 2
```
I spent a fair bit of time trying to understand this step of the build system but don't know how to proceed.

cmake --build build
cmake --install build --prefix install

gmake[1]: *** [CMakeFiles/Makefile2:910: src/mavsdk/core/CMakeFiles/generate_core_mavlink_xml_header.dir/all] Error 2
gmake: *** [Makefile:136: all] Error 2

answer_comments.body: Well the dependencies are built by the superbuild, so it shouldn't be too hard to find them. Here they are: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/third_party/CMakeLists.txt.

> I'm already submitting patches to upstream libraries.

We've upstreamed quite a few patches over the years. Some of them were just not accepted. For instance TinyXML did not want to support older CMake versions at all. Now maybe our patch is obsolete (do we still support CMake 3.10.2? That was for Ubuntu 18.04 which is EOL, so I'm guessing we can just remove this patch 🤔.

> From what I can tell, there is no place that MAVSDK actually checks out and builds TinyXML with superbuild disabled.

Because that's the whole point of a superbuild, isn't it? Either the superbuild builds the dependencies, or you handle them yourself 😇.

> Instead, it builds the superbuild, then re-uses the built dependencies again with superbuild disabled, which isn't really a fair build.

I don't understand what you mean here. If you disable the superbuild, it doesn't build the dependencies, period. It will still run `find_package` for them, and it is your responsibility to provide them.

> All the patches that MAVSDK is doing to upstream libraries need to get applied too.

Only those that apply to your platform and are necessary for your build, but yeah. Again, if you don't use our helpers, it's your responsibility. Always better when patches are not needed, and I'm happy whenever we can remove one 😊.

> Saying that we need to build with superbuild off to add a custom dialect

You don't need to build with superbuild off to add a custom dialect. There are many other ways, e.g.:

1. You can fork the repo and modify the two lines you need to modify in the MAVLink helper in third_party. That's literally a 2 lines change.
2. You can run the MAVSDK configure step with superbuild enabled, have your own step that replaces the locally-installed MAVLink with your custom one, and then proceed with the build step.

> large hurdle due to the large amount of undocumented customizations, patches, and other oddities done.

I don't know if this is the goal, but this kind of value judgment (and it happened in other messages as well) sounds offensive to me. Remember that I am doing this for free, in my free time. And unless you're paying @julianoes, he's doing it for free as well.

> Would you consider an approach of a hybrid superbuild that allows some packages available through find_package

Most definitely not, it is out of the question for me. You are complaining that our build is "odd", and in the next sentence you ask that we made it even more complicated just for your specific use-case. Either you use the superbuild, or you deal with the dependencies manually. And "dealing with the dependencies manually" means that you can just copy-paste all our helpers and use that. If you want to do it differently (in docker, in a shell script, in a python script, with a package manager), you're free to do so.

> At minimum. it appears safe to remove our third_party/tinyxml2/cmake-3.10.2.patch

It does indeed, thanks for the PR! 🚀 

> What I am getting at would that it would be helpful if there was a shell script, dockerfile, or CI file

From my point of view, it's all documented in code in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/third_party. I agree that the superbuild makes it harder to understand, but if you look at the individual CMakeLists for the dependencies, it's all really just like I describe in [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/).

Really, those contains exactly everything we need (including patches and compilation options) for the dependencies.

> would you consider making the URL and hash CMake options so I can supply those arguments at configure time rather than needing a fork? 

If you find a way to do it (I haven't looked into it), I say why not. My concern is that the superbuild scripts will make it convoluted. Again that is why I am now in favour of keeping the dependencies clearly separated from the project (again, [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/)) rather than having CMake build the dependencies as part of the project's configure step. This said, if we only provided helpers you would still have to somehow patch the MAVLink helper, so it would be similar to a fork/patch.

I would like to note that some of the "oddities" you find currently came exactly like this: "it makes it easier for the users if we do this automatically". So the happy path is just one command, but under the hood it adds complexity. That's why our CMake configure step requires python, for instance, because MAVLink needs it.

I am a bit of a purist here and came to think that we should simplify our build and delegate more to the users (making it their responsibility to understand how to build the dependencies, for instance). @julianoes is more pragmatic there, and I trust his judgement 😬.

> Perhaps it would help if I demonstrate what that would look like?

Why not, you would have to convince @julianoes here 😊. My way would be to remove the superbuild and just provide the helpers, and have users build like I describe [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/). I know e.g. gRPC offers some kind of hybrid way and I personally find that it just adds complexity.

comments.body: Before going into building your own custom dialect, may I ask if you considered using the MavlinkDirect plugin? It allows you to "inject" your own messages at runtime without having to rebuild MAVSDK.

> Before going into building your own custom dialect, may I ask if you considered using the MavlinkDirect plugin? It allows you to "inject" your own messages at runtime without having to rebuild MAVSDK.

Good question.

We need to make the XML regardless so that the tooling on the other components of our system speaks the same language.
We're going to want our GCS to be able to decode the data, our autopilot, our companion computer, and the developer tooling for log analysis, wireshark debugging, etc. Not all of them use MAVSDK. We are expecting a lot of custom messages, so we need something easy to keep changing.

The MavlinkDirect plugin approach could be an alternative, but I am concerned about the stability of it given the caution in the wiki.
Is this ready for production applications? Is it safe for a "mission critical" interface yet? The lack of enum support is annoying. At minimum, I'd try to get MAVSDK to import the message from an XML dialect rather than hard-coding the message definition in the C++ source code.

> Is this ready for production applications? Is it safe for a "mission critical" interface yet? 

Try it out and decide for yourself. The API is there to stay, maybe it'll change slightly but I think the design makes sense.
Does it have bugs, maybe. If you discover one, let me know and I'll try to fix it. If it's urgent and important, consider [sponsoring me](https://github.com/sponsors/julianoes) to move it up on my todo list.

> The lack of enum support is annoying.

It's a runtime thing, so there won't be native enums. That being said, we might be able to make enums using strings work. It'll just take some implementation. Again, up to you to contribute or convince me.
Are you open to improving compile time support for custom dialects?

> The lack of enum support is annoying.

By the way, I just checked and it looks like libmav (or our fork libmavlike) that we use for the xml parsing seems to have some support for enums, so it's a matter of integrating that into our API.

> Are you open to improving compile time support for custom dialects?

Like what? Not sure I understand what you mean.

> > Are you open to improving compile time support for custom dialects?
> 
> Like what? Not sure I understand what you mean.

I would like to point MAVSDK to my own local copy of the mavlink repo and when I compile mavsdk, have all dialects in my local fork built.
Currently, MAVSDK fetches and builds mavlink through ExternalProject_add which requires you to commit/push any changes to upstream.
I'd prefer an alternative approach such as `add_subdirectory` with a git submodule, or something like FetchContent , or even pulling in mavlink through find_package which any of these would allow you to easily change to a private fork of mavlink with custom messages and iterate quickly without having to commit/push.

This makes our custom messages driven off an XML file rather than JSON with compile time alignment with other tools in the ecosystem.

> I'd prefer an alternative approach such as add_subdirectory with a git submodule, or something like FetchContent , or even pulling in mavlink through find_package which any of these would allow you to easily change to a private fork of mavlink with custom messages and iterate quickly without having to commit/push.

We already have that: all our dependencies are pulled with `find_package`. We have a convoluted superbuild (I can say it because I wrote it 😬) which makes it look like a custom thing, but it is not. It's just that it's difficult to find a consensus between those who want a superbuild and those who don't, and whatever we choose we will always get complaints 🙈.

The way it works is that our superbuild builds all the dependencies separately and installs them locally. And it points CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to that location. Then the MAVSDK project uses `find_package` for all of the dependencies, the standard CMake way.

If you look at [how we build MAVLink](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt), you'll see that we [install it locally](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L39-L44), like all the other dependencies. Then we [`find_package(MAVLink required)`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5379eed714f2fc18acd142b9613bb3890702b8dd/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L4).

So you can totally point it to your own repo/hash (see [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/third_party/mavlink/CMakeLists.txt#L34-L35)):

```cmake
    ExternalProject_add(
        mavlink
        GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink
        GIT_TAG ${MAVLINK_GIT_HASH}
        PREFIX mavlink
```

I am against `add_subdirectory` and `FetchContent`, for multiple reasons, including because it only works with dependencies that support CMake. I detail my opinion in more details [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/) if you are interested. Though I wrote this superbuild, I am now against superbuilds in general and I explain my reasoning [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-superbuild/), again if you are interested.

> > I'd prefer an alternative approach such as add_subdirectory with a git submodule, or something like FetchContent , or even pulling in mavlink through find_package which any of these would allow you to easily change to a private fork of mavlink with custom messages and iterate quickly without having to commit/push.
> 
> We already have that: all our dependencies are pulled with `find_package`. We have a convoluted superbuild (I can say it because I wrote it 😬) which makes it look like a custom thing, but it is not. It's just that it's difficult to find a consensus between those who want a superbuild and those who don't, and whatever we choose we will always get complaints 🙈.

Then we [`find_package(MAVLink required)`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5379eed714f2fc18acd142b9613bb3890702b8dd/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L4).

If you want to allow using find_package, then why do you unconditionally fetch and build mavlink? If mavlink is already available in the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH, then you defeat the purpose of find_package. As mentioned above, I tried just using a local installed version that had my custom dialect, but MAVSDK ignored it. That is not expected for a typtical CMake project.

> That is not expected for a typtical CMake project.

You are right, but the root CMakeLists.txt is a *superbuild*. You should be able to disable it with [`-DSUPERBUILD=OFF`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt#L3) and handle the dependencies manually with `find_package`.

As mentioned above, I don't like superbuilds anymore, but many (most?) users don't want to handle the dependencies manually. Actually multiple times it has been requested that we provide some kind of one-liner because running the two cmake commands (configure + build) is not something that the users want to learn or copy from the README 🤷‍♂️. As I said, whatever we do we'll get complaints, we're just doing our best.

Just try with `-DSUPERBUILD=OFF`, hopefully it just works 👍.

Hi,

Fwiw, going back to your original question, I guess I am doing exactly what you are doing, a custom dialect added to a mavlink clone as xml. I also build without superbuild and make sure that MAVSDK cmake will find it, and then use a few MAVSDK cmake settings:

    -DMAVLINK_DIALECT:STRING="DialectCustom"
    -DSUPERBUILD=OFF
    -DMAVLink_DIR=$MAVLINK_SOURCE/install/lib/cmake/MAVLink
    -DMAVLINK_XML_PATH=$MAVLINK_SOURCE/message_definitions/v1.0

I am doing this for a number of years and works like a charm (for me at least).

So it does not "just work". There are undocumented dependencies. Here's a minimum dockerfile.
The [instructions](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build_linux.html#ubuntu) only declare dependencies if you are building a superbuild.
It would help if MAVSDK supplied the list of apt packages or steps to install source dependencies.
Or, MAVSDK could use a dependency manager such as `rosdep` to declare dependencies in a `package.xml`

```docker
FROM ubuntu:22.04

WORKDIR /ws

# https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build_linux.html

RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        git \
        python3 \
        python3-pip

RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/mavlink.git
WORKDIR /ws/mavlink
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive
RUN cmake -B build -S .
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install

WORKDIR /ws
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S . -DSUPERBUILD=OFF
```

I am well aware of the lack of funding, and unfortunately have never been in a position to fix that for the FOSS community. 

> > Would you consider an approach of a hybrid superbuild that allows some packages available through find_package
> 
> Most definitely not, it is out of the question for me. You are complaining that our build is "odd", and in the next sentence you ask that we made it even more complicated just for your specific use-case. Either you use the superbuild, or you deal with the dependencies manually. And "dealing with the dependencies manually" means that you can just copy-paste all our helpers and use that. If you want to do it differently (in docker, in a shell script, in a python script, with a package manager), you're free to do so.

Perhaps it would help if I demonstrate what that would look like? A lot of (small or big) projects do it, and I think it offers significant advantages for users in giving them the flexibility to rely on mavsdk to find dependencies they don't want to deal with but bring their own dependencies for the ones they want to change without requiring any source code changes to MAVSDK.

> At minimum. it appears safe to remove our third_party/tinyxml2/cmake-3.10.2.patch

It does indeed, thanks for the PR! 🚀 

> What I am getting at would that it would be helpful if there was a shell script, dockerfile, or CI file

From my point of view, it's all documented in code in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/third_party. I agree that the superbuild makes it harder to understand, but if you look at the individual CMakeLists for the dependencies, it's all really just like I describe in [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/).

Really, those contains exactly everything we need (including patches and compilation options) for the dependencies.

> would you consider making the URL and hash CMake options so I can supply those arguments at configure time rather than needing a fork? 

If you find a way to do it (I haven't looked into it), I say why not. My concern is that the superbuild scripts will make it convoluted. Again that is why I am now in favour of keeping the dependencies clearly separated from the project (again, [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/)) rather than having CMake build the dependencies as part of the project's configure step. This said, if we only provided helpers you would still have to somehow patch the MAVLink helper, so it would be similar to a fork/patch.

I would like to note that some of the "oddities" you find currently came exactly like this: "it makes it easier for the users if we do this automatically". So the happy path is just one command, but under the hood it adds complexity. That's why our CMake configure step requires python, for instance, because MAVLink needs it.

I am a bit of a purist here and came to think that we should simplify our build and delegate more to the users (making it their responsibility to understand how to build the dependencies, for instance). @julianoes is more pragmatic there, and I trust his judgement 😬.

> Perhaps it would help if I demonstrate what that would look like?

Why not, you would have to convince @julianoes here 😊. My way would be to remove the superbuild and just provide the helpers, and have users build like I describe [here](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/). I know e.g. gRPC offers some kind of hybrid way and I personally find that it just adds complexity.
Sorry, I lost the thread here? What else needs doing?

verified.note: Docs PR merged addresses the title, but thread continues with unresolved build-tooling asks and ends with the maintainer saying 'I lost the thread here, what else needs doing?'.

If you could provide instructions how I can reproduce it that would be helpful.

And `main` doesn't look quite right either... :thinking:

comments.body: Same issue [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1917). Author was unable to reproduce and we got around it by just using mavlink passthrough call to request all params. It's not as eloquent because we just use a timeout to determine when we've "should" have received all params. For us it was on startup connection so the delay in receiving the params was not an issue.

Thanks for the report.

title: CMake local install RPATH missing
author: Ryanf55
body:
I tried consuming a locally installed version of MAVSDK in another package's install, and MAVSDK's CMake target fails to correctly export the shared library destination on an installed target.
I suspected this is an rpath issue, and spent 2 hours trying various recommendations, but have not found a solution.
Here is a conference talk from a CMake maintainer specifically about this use case with rpath:
https://youtu.be/m0DwB4OvDXk?si=3TaOFA6OdxY4z5F6&t=2452

I tried his recommendation on MAVSDK, and that did not fix the issue.

To reproduce, here's a Dockerfile:

```docker
FROM ubuntu:22.04

WORKDIR /ws

# https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build_linux.html

RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        git \
        python3 \
        python3-pip

RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
RUN cmake --build build -j8
# Install is slightly different not using the install target, but it's the same idea.
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install


RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        pkg-config \
        astyle \
        bluez \
        bluez-tools \
        libbluetooth-dev

WORKDIR /ws
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules --branch cmake-install https://github.com/ryanf55/RemoteIDTransmitter.git
WORKDIR /ws/RemoteIDTransmitter
RUN CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/ws/MAVSDK/install cmake -B build
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
RUN ./install/bin/rid-transmitter
```

Just run `docker build . --progress=plain` and you will eventually get 
```
 > [stage-0 17/17] RUN ./install/bin/rid-transmitter:
0.378 ./install/bin/rid-transmitter: error while loading shared libraries: libmavsdk.so.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

The example here is when I tried using an installed executable that links to MAVSDK.
The linkage to MAVSDK is using the standard target_link_libraries approach:
https://github.com/Ryanf55/RemoteIDTransmitter/blob/cmake-install/CMakeLists.txt#L37


FYI @dakejahl

RUN CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/ws/MAVSDK/install cmake -B build
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
RUN ./install/bin/rid-transmitter

> [stage-0 17/17] RUN ./install/bin/rid-transmitter:
0.378 ./install/bin/rid-transmitter: error while loading shared libraries: libmavsdk.so.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

comments.body:
> ```
> # Install is slightly different not using the install target, but it's the same idea.
> RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
> ```

Why? Isn't this the root cause? Why can't you use the `--target install` as it is intended?

> > ```
> > # Install is slightly different not using the install target, but it's the same idea.
> > RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
> > ```
> 
> Why? Isn't this the root cause? Why can't you use the `--target install` as it is intended?

No, you get the same error, the only difference is one allows you to set the install location at install time, while the other requires to decide during configure time. For this example, it has no effect.

First, a quick fix: you can set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`:

```
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/ ./install/bin/rid-transmitter
```

> I tried his recommendation on MAVSDK, and that did not fix the issue.

What did you try? Note that I didn't watch the video.

I would be tempted to try something like this:

```patch
diff --git a/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt b/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt
index 6392ba41..73f6194e 100644
--- a/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -130,10 +130,19 @@ else()
     )
 endif()
 
+if(IS_ABSOLUTE "${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
+    set(MAVSDK_INSTALL_RPATH "${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
+else()
+    set(MAVSDK_INSTALL_RPATH "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
+endif()
+
 set_target_properties(mavsdk PROPERTIES
     VERSION ${MAVSDK_VERSION_STRING}
     SOVERSION ${MAVSDK_SOVERSION_STRING}
+    INSTALL_RPATH "${MAVSDK_INSTALL_RPATH}"
+    INSTALL_RPATH_USE_LINK_PATH TRUE
 )
+
 if (MSVC)
     set_target_properties(mavsdk PROPERTIES
         DEBUG_POSTFIX "d"
```

Now if I build it with:

```
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=install -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
cmake --build build --target install
```

Then the rpath is correct and it works with your `rid-transmitter`:

```
# readelf -d /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.10.2 | grep RUNPATH
 0x000000000000001d (RUNPATH)            Library runpath: [/ws/MAVSDK/install/lib]
```

The problem with your `cmake --install build --prefix install` is then that it sets the install path at install time, though the rpath is set at build time. So the way you call it, it would result in the wrong rpath anyway, because my patch above relies on `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX`.

```
# readelf -d /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.10.2 | grep RUNPATH
 0x000000000000001d (RUNPATH)            Library runpath: [/usr/local/lib]
```

Now one may argue that it is good enough to have it set with `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX`, and if you really need to change the install path at install time with `--prefix`, then you can manually set the rpath with something like:

```
patchelf --set-rpath /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.10.2
```

Or set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

@Ryanf55: what do you think? Does that correspond to what your video says? Maybe there is a better way that works with setting the `--prefix` at install time, but my guess is that CMake won't go change the binary at this step, so it's too late to change the runpath.

I actually watched the video you linked above, and it is a very nice presentation 😊. However, I don't think that setting the rpath to $ORIGIN will solve this particular problem you have. It would help MAVSDK find its own dependencies, but in your case the problem is about `rid-transmitter` not finding MAVSDK.

When you have your issue, the `ldd` output looks like this:

```
# ldd install/bin/rid-transmitter 
	linux-vdso.so.1 (0x00007fe0137ef000)
	libmavsdk.so.3 => not found
	libbluetooth.so.3 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libbluetooth.so.3 (0x00007fe013753000)
	libstdc++.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 (0x00007fe013400000)
	libm.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6 (0x00007fe01366c000)
	libgcc_s.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgcc_s.so.1 (0x00007fe01364c000)
	libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x00007fe013000000)
	/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007fe0137f1000)
```

It could build against MAVSDK, but at runtime the dynamic linker doesn't know where to find it because libmavsdk.so.3 did not have a runpath set and is installed in a custom location.

My understanding is that the $ORIGIN trick would help your executable. Maybe it's easier to show with an example. You have this issue:

```sh
# ./install/bin/rid-transmitter 
./install/bin/rid-transmitter: error while loading shared libraries: libmavsdk.so.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

Say you copy `libmavsdk.so.3` next to `rid-transmitter` and set the runpath to $ORIGIN, then it will work:

```
# cp /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3 /ws/RemoteIDTransmitter/install/bin/
# patchelf --set-rpath '$ORIGIN' /ws/RemoteIDTransmitter/install/bin/rid-transmitter

# ./install/bin/rid-transmitter 
Parsing failed:
File could not be opened for reading
	(error occurred at line 0, column 0 of '/root/.local/share/rid-transmitter/config.toml')
```

I am assuming that the "Parsing failed" error is orthogonal to the dynamic linking issue we're discussing now 🙈.

So you can use $ORIGIN in order to find dependencies next to your binary, but setting it into your dependencies won't help you in this case.

What about these three workarounds:

1. Install into `/usr`:

```
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S. -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr
RUN cmake --build build -j8
RUN cmake --build build --target install
```

2. Install into `/usr/local` (which is the cmake default):

```
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
RUN cmake --build build -j8
RUN cmake --build build --target install
```

3. Install using wget/dpkg

```
RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        git \
        wget

RUN wget https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v3.10.2/libmavsdk-dev_3.10.2_ubuntu22.04_amd64.deb
RUN dpkg -i libmavsdk-dev_3.10.2_ubuntu22.04_amd64.deb
```

> What about these three workarounds

Those will work because they install MAVSDK on the system. I think the original issue is that they want to install MAVSDK locally and use it from there.

The more I think about it, the more I believe that the solution is to either use LD_LIBRARY_PATH or manually `patchelf`:

```
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
RUN cmake --build build -j8
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
patchelf --set-rpath /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.10.2
```

Because MAVSDK cannot guess the final use-case and should probably not leak paths of the build machine. The package knows how it will be used and can set the runpath after installation (with `patchelf --set-rpath`).
There was no more follow up. I assume this is good enough and I'm closing this. Please comment again if I'm wrong.

verified.note: textbook null case: maintainer engaged at length with workarounds but OP never confirmed if any worked (unmerged PR); fully Docker-reproducible per issue's own Dockerfile

title: Problem with TCP connection to a PX4 SITL
author: ZhenyuShiUAV
body:
Hi, I'm trying to connect to a PX4 SITL through TCP as a simulator, but when I'm using the line ```c++ ConnectionResult connection_result = mavsdk.add_any_connection(argv[1]); ``` with the argument for tcp: ``` tcp://:4560 ``` I got this following error ``` [02:56:01|Error] connect error: Connection refused (tcp_connection.cpp:87) ``` I also tried `tcp://127.0.0.1:4560`, same result. And I can connect to the PX4 through UDP.

To figure out the problem, I also tried using python code ```python connection = mavutil.mavlink_connection('tcpin:127.0.0.1:4560') ``` which actually worked and I can see this line in the PX4 SITL terminal ``` INFO [simulator] Simulator connected on TCP port 4560. ``` and I tried with `'tcpin:127.0.0.1:4560'` to `'tcp:127.0.0.1:4560'`, which is ```python connection = mavutil.mavlink_connection('tcp:127.0.0.1:4560') ``` and I got the error ``` [Errno 111] Connection refused sleeping ``` which is similar to what I got for the C++ tcp connection.

FYI, I'm a debug build for MAVSDK, and the tcp connection line is from the takeoff_and_land example code. For what I'm working on, it would be more convenient for me to stay with C++. Am I doing something wrong and how can I fix this? Thank you.

answer_comments.body:
> is there any example for setting up a TCP server with C++?

MAVSDK does not support being a TCP server. Only a TCP client.
@PuvaneshRam sounds like an AirSim and not MAVSDK issue to me.

If you see:

> Waiting for simulator to accept connection on TCP port 4560.

This means PX4 is not communicating correctly with AirSim. This has nothing to do with MAVSDK.

title: MAVSDK-Python / examples / camera.py doesn't work
author: takata1021
body:
I'm running typhoon_h480 or plane_cam from the Gazebo simulator and running the MavSDK camera.py.
The camera class will result in an error.
You can shoot with the camera from QGroundControl.
Is it possible to operate the camera from the Mav SDK while the Gazebo simulator is running? Please tell me how to do it.
Is this a bug?
resolution_evidence: thread converges on a working answer

answer_comments.body: When you take a picture from QGroundControl it just grabs a picture from the stream and saves it, as far as I remember.

> A camera is only sometimes discovered.

Hmm that's weird... I think it relies on the heartbeat, so would it mean that the camera heartbeat is unreliable? Just guessing here.

> I have no idea where the image is saved to?

It is not, it delegates that to you. What MAVSDK will give you is the URLs to access the pictures/video streams (see below).

> Another thing, how do I actually access the picture/ video frames from MAVSDK? 

When you take a picture, you receive a [`CaptureInfo` that contains a `file_url`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L314). If your drone exposes e.g. an HTTP server, that's the URL where you can get the picture. So you want to [`SubscribeCaptureInfo`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/8966cf59029ac17d81654071ca6d3d27f0d8897d/protos/camera/camera.proto#L75) here, or [`ListPhotos`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/8966cf59029ac17d81654071ca6d3d27f0d8897d/protos/camera/camera.proto#L59) to list all of them.

For the video stream, with the [`VideoStreamSettings` you get a `video_stream_uri`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L324). Typically that would be an `rtsp://` address that you can use to access the video. So you want to use [`SubscribeVideoStreamInfo`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L71) to get that.
I'm working on getting some of th camera/stream functionality developed. Stay tuned. Although for "server" plugins there is not a lot of support in languages other than X..

There has been lots of work around camera server.

There is also this example: https://github.com/julianoes/siyi-a8-mini-camera-manager

1) A camera is only *sometimes* discovered. I had to run the code a few times before I actually connected to a camera. Not sure why this would be?
2) I have no idea where the image is saved to? Another thing, how do I actually access the picture/ video frames from MAVSDK? Is this supported?

Thanks in advance!

> A camera is only sometimes discovered.

Hmm that's weird... I think it relies on the heartbeat, so would it mean that the camera heartbeat is unreliable? Just guessing here.

> I have no idea where the image is saved to?

It is not, it delegates that to you. What MAVSDK will give you is the URLs to access the pictures/video streams (see below).

> Another thing, how do I actually access the picture/ video frames from MAVSDK? 

When you take a picture, you receive a [`CaptureInfo` that contains a `file_url`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L314). If your drone exposes e.g. an HTTP server, that's the URL where you can get the picture. So you want to [`SubscribeCaptureInfo`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/8966cf59029ac17d81654071ca6d3d27f0d8897d/protos/camera/camera.proto#L75) here, or [`ListPhotos`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/8966cf59029ac17d81654071ca6d3d27f0d8897d/protos/camera/camera.proto#L59) to list all of them.

For the video stream, with the [`VideoStreamSettings` you get a `video_stream_uri`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L324). Typically that would be an `rtsp://` address that you can use to access the video. So you want to use [`SubscribeVideoStreamInfo`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/main/protos/camera/camera.proto#L71) to get that.
I'm working on getting some of th camera/stream functionality developed. Stay tuned. Although for "server" plugins there is not a lot of support in languages other than X..

There has been lots of work around camera server.

There is also this example: https://github.com/julianoes/siyi-a8-mini-camera-manager

verified.note: No maintainer confirmation of an actual fix; users found workarounds outside MAVSDK (GStreamer/OpenCV) while the core question stays open.

title: MAVSDK timeout tuning

answer_comments.body:
This should be enough:
```
cmake --build build/default -j8 && build/default/src/integration_tests/integration_tests_runner --gtest_filter="SitlTest.MissionTransferLossy"
```

5 or 10 seconds seems way too high, it likely won't work because PX4 on the other side still assumes a timeout much lower, around 0.5 seconds. What is the ping/latency between MAVSDK and PX4 for your setup?

> I might be wrong but I assumed the timeout function told PX4 what timeout to expect?

No, it's really on the MAVSDK side: it tells MAVSDK which timeout to use. You are right that it would make sense to synchronize that value with PX4, but MAVLink does not provide that, and I don't know what it would imply on the PX4 side (and how one would handle the case where PX4 does not support it).

title: Clarify FollowMe::Config::min_height_m and follow_dist_m
author: hamishwillee
body:
This states:
```
float min_height_m = 8.0f - Min follow height, in meters.
```
My guess would be that this is actually not minimum follow height, but actual/desired follow height. So when we specify a target position (e.g. 0 AMSL) the height that the drone will follow will be 8m above that - correct?

If so, then this should be renamed `follow_height_m`.

1. Can we set negative values? i.e. to follow from below/under a target?

We should also rename `follow_dist_m ` to `follow_distance_m` for consistency.

answer_comments.body:
> I think DroneCore would have to use the same xml file for parameter limits in order to know these values. Right now that's not the case so I would vote to have a safe default and make sure this is tested in CI soon.

It can never know them even with xml file, because they can be changed via GCS.  I'm OK with having a safe default as long as we actually set it - as it is now you can get an inconsistency between the vehicle set value and dronecode. If we're going to set it though, then why not make it a configurable default?

> I vote to change names to human readable such as distance since we don't have the same 16 char parameter length constraints.

+1

>> If we're going to set it though, then why not make it a configurable default?

> @hamishwillee sorry I didn't get your point about making default configuration. As said earlier, we already have default configuration set, regardless of current PX4 configuration.

At the moment we just set some value DroneCode side to control what we send to the vehicle. We don't care what  PX4 has set. @julianoes suggested having a sensible minimum - and I hope he means that we should write that minimum to the vehicle (?).
What I am saying is that if we're going to be writing a parameter to the vehicle anyway, lets make it something that can be set through the API.  We can't know what are sensible minimums for all use cases.
Yes. Does this override actually change the min height on the vehicle?

comments.body:
> My guess would be that this is actually not minimum follow height, but actual/desired follow height. So when we specify a target position (e.g. 0 AMSL) the height that the drone will follow will be 8m above that - correct?
>
Yes. I understood so from [PX4 Follow Me guide](https://docs.px4.io/en/flight_modes/follow_me.html#configuration).

> Can we set negative values? i.e. to follow from below/under a target?
>
As per [PX4 Full Parameter Reference for Follow target](https://docs.px4.io/en/advanced_config/parameter_reference.html#follow-target), `NAV_MIN_FT_HT` is of type `float`; and we can't set negative values: **Min: 8.0 meters**.
> If so, then this should be renamed follow_height_m.
>
> We should also rename follow_dist_m to follow_distance_m for consistency.
>
Sure we can. I wanted to keep it consistent with PX4 parameter names as people may be familiar with them.

@shakthi-prashanth-m @julianoes Thank you. Now I explore this in detail, I think our implementation of the minimums and config is wrong.

What we do now is have hard coded minimum values for the various follow parameters. These match whatever the documented default [follow-me parameter values](https://docs.px4.io/en/advanced_config/parameter_reference.html#follow-target) are in PX4. So for example, the minimum follow height is set, by default, to 8 metres. We allow a user to set whatever height they like in the config but they will be constrained to the minimum.

The problems with this are:
- Anyone can change the value of these parameters on PX4 at any time. A user might then be unable to reach a value that is supported on PX4, or might request a value that is below the minimum, but we won't get warning
- The value is hard coded so changing requires a recompile.

What I think we should do is fetch these minimum values from the PX4 parameters rather than hard coding. 
We might also allow the value to be set through the API, though that is optional.
Last of all, the config value should be changed to reflect that it is the desired height, not a minimum height.

Make sense?

@hamishwillee I agree a user can change follow-me config from QGroundControl. When user sets value out-of-range, he/she will be warned as below.

![follow_me_height_change](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26615772/34142119-66fb95a2-e4ab-11e7-8448-caf3424696ca.png)

>Anyone can change the value of these parameters on PX4 at any time. A user might then be unable to reach a value that is supported on PX4, or might request a value that is below the minimum, but we won't get warning
>
What we fetch from PX4 may not be minimum values. But may be changed to different values outside (for. eg: from QGroundControl).
>What I think we should do is fetch these minimum values from the PX4 parameters rather than hard coding.
>
We ensure that we start with default Follow Me configuration by applying default parameters during [Follow Me startup](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/plugins/follow_me/follow_me_impl.cpp#L176). I believe that it is safer approach than fetching current PX4 configuration. We can choose what is right way here.

> We ensure that we start with default Follow Me configuration by applying default parameters during Follow Me startup. 

That is a valid alternative too. In that case though, we should make them something that is set as part of Config.
I don't have a strong opinion about which approach is better. Maybe @julianoes does.
@shakthi-prashanth-m @julianoes Did you guys agree what needs to be done with this?

I think DroneCore would have to use the same xml file for parameter limits in order to know these values. Right now that's not the case so I would vote to have a safe default and make sure this is tested in CI soon.

I vote to change names to human readable such as `distance` since we don't have the same 16 char parameter length constraints.

> I think DroneCore would have to use the same xml file for parameter limits in order to know these values. Right now that's not the case so I would vote to have a safe default and make sure this is tested in CI soon.

It can never know them even with xml file, because they can be changed via GCS.  I'm OK with having a safe default as long as we actually set it - as it is now you can get an inconsistency between the vehicle set value and dronecode. If we're going to set it though, then why not make it a configurable default?

> I vote to change names to human readable such as distance since we don't have the same 16 char parameter length constraints.

+1

> I vote to change names to human readable such as distance since we don't have the same 16 char parameter length constraints.
>
I shall make changes.

>> If we're going to set it though, then why not make it a configurable default?

> @hamishwillee sorry I didn't get your point about making default configuration. As said earlier, we already have default configuration set, regardless of current PX4 configuration.

At the moment we just set some value DroneCode side to control what we send to the vehicle. We don't care what  PX4 has set. @julianoes suggested having a sensible minimum - and I hope he means that we should write that minimum to the vehicle (?).
What I am saying is that if we're going to be writing a parameter to the vehicle anyway, lets make it something that can be set through the API.  We can't know what are sensible minimums for all use cases.

OK, Yes. Although we set default PX4 Follow Me configuration to start with; users can always [override existing configuration](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/integration_tests/follow_me.cpp#L113) before starting Follow Me (optional).
Yes. Does this override actually change the min height on the vehicle?
@hamishwillee  Yes it does.
Awesome. I'll go disappear then :-)

verified.note: Linked PR 217 ('Add Follow me example') doesn't match the requested rename; thread never confirms follow_height_m/follow_distance_m were actually renamed.

title: Getting HTTP 503 when attempting to subscribe to telemetry but works after connecting with QGroundControl
author: tltanlum
body:
When I connect with `mavsdk_server_bin` to my drone running `ArduPilot`, I cannot subscribe for telemetry as my web client is receiving 503 from `mavsdk_server_bin`. It is the same behavior with `APM Planner` and I connect through the serial port in both cases(`mavsdk_server_bin` and `APM Planner`) mutually exclusively.

Once I connect with `QGroundControl` through the serial port, all the data starts streaming. From there on I can connect with either `APM Planner` or `mavsdk_server_bin` and they both receive the data just fine; and my web client can subscribe to telemetry just fine through `mavsdk_server_bin`.

I am not sure what triggers the data to start streaming through `QGroundControl `and I would expect this to be the norm to be honest. I am wondering if there is an `ArduPilot` setting to have this behavior enabled by default for all clients connecting to `mavlink` through serial/tcp/udp?

If I hardware reset the `ArduPilot` the same problem comes up as I need to run `QGroundControl` which somehow triggers the `mavlink` streaming.

APM-Planner v2-2.0.30-rc3
QGrountControl v4.3.0
MAVSDK-Server v2.9.1

Thank you!

What web client is that? How do you connect to mavsdk_server_bin exactly?

title: Camera plugin to implement MAVLink Camera Protocol client interface
author: shakthi-prashanth-m
body:
Its is required to add a plugin to configure Camera as per https://mavlink.io/en/protocol/camera.html to interface Camera Streaming Daemon.

To start with, Camera plugin should 
- [x] listen to heartbeat from Camera component
- [x] get basic camera information
- [x] configure camera settings
- [x] send start image capture
- [x] send stop image capture
- [x] get information about captured image

UPDATE:
@julianoes added camera plugin as part of #338 Its WIP. Thanks @julianoes .

I would add on top of it:
- [ ] start video streaming
- [ ] request video stream info
- [ ] configure video streaming
- [ ] stop video streaming

answer_comments.body:
> @julianoes, with multiple component support in DroneCore, we can use same port for autopilot and camera isn't it ?

Yes, we can but it all depends on how it is all set up. For Yuneec's case, e.g. the camera and autopilot are on the same UDP port because the autopilot communicates "through" the camera.

> We don't request for Autopilot version if Heartbeat has MAV_TYPE_CAMERA, etc ?

Correct, we shouldn't.

> Regarding UDP connections, there may be multiple scenarios that need to be considered.

Right. I'm not sure where 3. is needed though.

> Autopilot and camera should then have both the same system ID but different component IDs. As @shakthi-prashanth-m suggested we need proper support for multiple components (#304).

A camera will be associated with a device and share its system ID. Do we need to consider systems where a mavlink camera might exist separately from a device?

> I think we shouldn't have the streaming logic in the same diagram as the camera definition. They don't really depend on each, I think.

Jumping back a big, I agree with @julianoes on the above. Even if camera vs streaming operations can be handled together I think it makes sense for readers to see them separately.
As an aside - CSD does not yet support video capture. We can still define the interface, but they won't work yet.

linked_prs.title: common.xml: Correct default values of SET_VIDEO_STREAM_SETTINGS

comments.body: I can add start, stop, captured image.

1. We should also consider fetching the [Camera Definition File](https://mavlink.io/en/protocol/camera_def.html) - advanced camera information
2. The Camera Streaming Daemon also supports RTSP streams and (optionally) stream discovery (via Avahi). This probably isn't part of the same API, but we should consider if there is any sensible Dronecore integration point for that too.

PS and probably we should rename this "Camera plugin to interface MAVLink Camera Protocol". The CSD is just one possible implementation of that protocol. Much of this might even work directly on a PX4 based camera.

I think diagram is ok to illustrate how a plugin works but I can tell you the steps aren't going to be the same on every camera or product that integrates a camera, I would love to see this implemented in a way that every product vendor could extend this abstract camera plugin and build on top of it, @julianoes would this (abstract camera class) work with your implementation? is this useful?

@mrpollo , every camera vendor should support MAVLink Camera protocol. So camera plugin is essentially a client to  MAVLink Camera protocol compliment server.  I didn't get your point about abstract camera class.

I discussed with Lalit earlier he said it's WIP about MAVLink commands for video streaming but streaming feature itself exists. 

I see that command for getting video streaming info already exists: 
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_VIDEO_STREAM_INFORMATION in response to which CSD should return 
https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#VIDEO_STREAM_INFORMATION.

If they are WIP, I am fine to work on it so that camera plugin can do video streaming.

Sounds good.

The only bit that perhaps is a real question is the parsing of the camera definition and the way that the parameters are set. We might want to design our implementation to allow a manufacturer to provide a nicer layer over that bit for their own camera.

@shakthi-prashanth-m

1. I think the target should be provide generic camera interfaces as a part of SDK, interfaces that would comply with MAVLink Camera Protocol (as @hamishwillee suggested, rename the task to "Camera plugin to interface MAVLink Camera Protocol")
2. MAVLink Camera Protocol  is not specific to any camera. Hence, the interfaces based on the protocol would also be generic. Nevertheless, it should still be possible to design it in a way so as to enable vendors to extend the plugin or customize in the way they want (as @mrpollo suggested)
3. To test the interfaces, we can run Camera Server (CSD) at the vehicle end.
4. MAVLink commands for video streaming were WIP and perhaps outdated now. I will take a relook on what needs to be done for these msgs. I would suggest skip WIP messages unless you want to first work on making them mainline, which would be an effort taking your focus away from camera plugin work
5. Can you add an initial PR with basic camera functionality?
@lbegani OK Sure. I'll add it soon. Thanks.

I think we shouldn't have the streaming logic in the same diagram as the camera definition. They don't really depend on each, I think.

As said before, I'll add the camera definition part and simple camera commands because I already have begun that work internally.

Therefore, it would be great if @shakthi-prashanth-m can add the streaming stuff since I don't know how that works.

@julianoes I am not sure if it makes sense to add camera features before the basic infrastructure for camera is there in the SDK. @shakthi-prashanth-m and myself started working on this. Can you publish your proposal or WIP code?

I will push it as soon as I get to it.

However, I don't think you depend on the basic functionality that I provide though.

Camera Plugin must define interfaces for the following - 
- [ ] Discover Camera Components (heartbeats)
- [ ] Get/Process Camera Information
- [ ] Get/Process Storage Information
- [ ] Fetch Camera Definition File
- [ ] Parse and export the parameters and its possible values
- [ ] Get/Set/Reset Parameters
- [ ] Start/Stop Image Capture
- [ ] Start/Stop Video Capture
Kind of. What if there are multiple cameras (and yes, that is a realistic scenario).

```
drone_conn.add_udp_connection(14540);    // 14540 for autopilot
camera_conna.add_udp_connection(24540);  // 24540 for camera
```
Both autopilot and camera component send the heartbeat to same UDP port (14550)

I think, we can't use `DroneCore `class for handling camera connection. Because, we handle only Autopilot MAVLink messages in `core `and we need to handle whole camera connection handling in plugin itself.
>What if there are multiple cameras

Yes, we have to handle multiple cameras as well, so it makes sense to do discover, connect, etc in camera plugin itself rather than re-using `DroneCore `class for that. In that case, how does it become DroneCore plugin ? :) Of-course, DroneCore applications can use it. But that is even possible if it exists outside as well.  Isn't it ?

>Both autopilot and camera component send the heartbeat to same UDP port (14550)

Right now, we can't listen on the same port for both autopilot and camera. So, we have to choose another well-known port say, 14550. (We have to make sure not to launch QGC same time).

I think it should look like that:
```
DroneCore dc;

dc.add_udp_connection(14540);    // for autopilot
dc.add_udp_connection(24540);  // for camera
```

Autopilot and camera should then have both the same system ID but different component IDs. As @shakthi-prashanth-m suggested we need proper support for multiple components (#304).

For the case of multiple camera, we use more UDP connections if required, and we distinguish them by component ID, see:
http://mavlink.org/messages/common#MAV_COMP_ID_CAMERA
http://mavlink.org/messages/common#MAV_COMP_ID_CAMERA2
etc.

I agree that we distinguish camera components by component id.
>For the case of multiple camera, we use more UDP connections if required,


All camera components deal with a single UDP port, I think. Consider, CSD for example. It will use port 14550 for all camera components. @lbegani is that right ?

@julianoes, with multiple component support in DroneCore, we can use same port for autopilot and camera isn't it ? We don't request for Autopilot version if Heartbeat has `MAV_TYPE_CAMERA`, etc ?

Regarding UDP connections, there may be multiple scenarios that need to be considered. We may not to support all of them
1. Both autopilot and camera components sending mavlink messages to same port
2. Autopilot to one port (X), camera components to another port (Y)
3. Autopilot to one port (X), camera component to different ports (Y,Z, ...)

> @julianoes, with multiple component support in DroneCore, we can use same port for autopilot and camera isn't it ?

Yes, we can but it all depends on how it is all set up. For Yuneec's case, e.g. the camera and autopilot are on the same UDP port because the autopilot communicates "through" the camera.

> We don't request for Autopilot version if Heartbeat has MAV_TYPE_CAMERA, etc ?

Correct, we shouldn't.

> Regarding UDP connections, there may be multiple scenarios that need to be considered.

Right. I'm not sure where 3. is needed though.

> Autopilot and camera should then have both the same system ID but different component IDs. As @shakthi-prashanth-m suggested we need proper support for multiple components (#304).

A camera will be associated with a device and share its system ID. Do we need to consider systems where a mavlink camera might exist separately from a device?

> I think we shouldn't have the streaming logic in the same diagram as the camera definition. They don't really depend on each, I think.

Jumping back a big, I agree with @julianoes on the above. Even if camera vs streaming operations can be handled together I think it makes sense for readers to see them separately.
As an aside - CSD does not yet support video capture. We can still define the interface, but they won't work yet.
@shakthi-prashanth-m can we close this?
Yes, we can! And it is already closed :-)

verified.note: base camera protocol landed via #338 but the stretch goals (video streaming) were never completed; closed as 'good enough' not clearly fixed. Also plugin API is testable against simulated MAVLink camera, not just hardware

title: Yaw/heading not accessible in MissionItem class
author: mwshafer
body:
It seems that `MissionItems` don't include a vehicle heading, which would be really helpful. This could be accomplished by adding the following methods to the `MissionItem` class:

- `yaw_to()` (double degrees from N): Rotate the vehicle to the specified angle after reaching position set by `set_position()`.
- `yaw_for()` (double seconds): Rotate the vehicle for the specified time after reaching position set by `set_position()` at rate specified by `set_yaw_rate()`.
- `set_yaw_rate()` (double rotation speed in deg/s): Set the target rotation rate for vehicle yawing. 
- `set_yaw_departure_ned` (double degrees from N): Set the heading for after mission item (transition to next mission item)

I am not sure the last method would be needed if the heading specified by `yaw_to()` could be maintainted between waypoints. If it could, the last item would be redundant. If multiple headings are desired at a given position, they could simply be stacked as a series of mission items with the same position, but differing values set by `yaw_to()`. 

I have a project wherein we need to be able to specify the vehicle heading because we have a directional antenna attached. I'd like to transition to Mavsdk, but need this heading control capacity.

answer_comments.body:
I'm currently working on refactoring the mission transfer (#964) in order to make it easier to change the mission plugin and also add things like geofence, rally point upload etc.

Once that's done we can surely revisit the yaw settings, it should then be less overwhelming to change it. And as an alternative you could also use the `mission_raw` plugin which allows any sort of MAVLink mission items.

The `mission_raw` plugin is currently a bit crippled because it only implements download but not upload but that will change after the refactor:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/c5404eb7ca88b6a404b82154d7ad49b3cc6b7d17/src/plugins/mission_raw/include/plugins/mission_raw/mission_raw.h#L100-L108

> I see you removed the 'feature request' tag and added the 'feature' tag to this issue.

I was just consolidating the tags. Once we are done with the auto-generation we can consider handling yaw better in the mission plugin. Until then we can only recommend to use mission_raw which should have most features as of the next release.

Looks like there is yaw:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/blob/34bce6d61dba5f72b602bdbd31f04fceff093881/protos/mission/mission.proto#L210

comments.body: Would you prefer the vehicle to always have the heading set to a specific direction or only at waypoints? The reason that we usually fly "forward" to the next waypoint is because we generally have obstacle avoidance facing forward and can then use gimbals to look around if required.

I think that maybe by default, MAVSDK could use the fly "forward" feature that you mentioned for the reasons you highlighted. The `set_yaw_departure()` would be used to override that feature only if the mission designer requires it. The documentation would just need a notice that obstacle avoidance sensors wouldn't be pointed in the direction of flight if that feature is used. What do you think?

If this gets added in phases, for me, the first three of the methods listed are most crucial. I listed them in order of necessity. The last one would be really helpful eventually, but isn't absolutely critical. I am still new to this open source development process. How long do you think adding such features might take? Thanks!

I just realized that a `set_yaw_dir` would also be needed to specify the direction of rotation. The direction of rotation could alternatively, be set using a second input argument in the `yaw_to` and `yaw_for` methods.

> The last one would be really helpful eventually, but isn't absolutely critical. I am still new to this open source development process. How long do you think adding such features might take?

@mwshafer, that's a good question. This is an open source project so no one has to do anything as such. And whoever needs something will have to make a pull request and contribute what they need. 
This being said, us developers we are interested in making people get use out of the software / be successful with it and we therefore often fix what is broken and add what is asked for. Also, we don't always jump straight to implementation in order to encourage participation or contributions.

The timeline for a feature then depends on what else is going on, how many developers ask for something, and how well it is aligned with what the project should enable and what we as maintainers need anyway for their own/internal projects.

For this specific feature I would argue that it is not unreasonable and something that will come up for others as well at some point. Therefore, it makes sense to add it in the next few weeks, at least that is my goal but I can't promise it.

@julianoes Do you know if this as seen any development. I am working on a funding proposal and was recently thinking about yawing flight modes or control again. Just thought I would check in and reiterate that this would be extremely helpful. Thanks!

I'm currently working on refactoring the mission transfer (#964) in order to make it easier to change the mission plugin and also add things like geofence, rally point upload etc.

Once that's done we can surely revisit the yaw settings, it should then be less overwhelming to change it. And as an alternative you could also use the `mission_raw` plugin which allows any sort of MAVLink mission items.
Great to hear! I'll check in on the `mission_raw ` plugin. Thanks.

The `mission_raw` plugin is currently a bit crippled because it only implements download but not upload but that will change after the refactor:

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/c5404eb7ca88b6a404b82154d7ad49b3cc6b7d17/src/plugins/mission_raw/include/plugins/mission_raw/mission_raw.h#L100-L108

I don't know how to handle that...i.e., MissionRaw::MavlinkMissionItemInt::param4. 
Would somebody explain that?

> I'm currently working on refactoring the mission transfer (#964) in order to make it easier to change the mission plugin and also add things like geofence, rally point upload etc.
> 
> Once that's done we can surely revisit the yaw settings, it should then be less overwhelming to change it. And as an alternative you could also use the `mission_raw` plugin which allows any sort of MAVLink mission items.

Hi! Hope you all are alright! Ah, #964 seems to be merged into dev now :) great! Do you already have any plan or schedule to extend the `MissionItem` to include yaw and the other stuff when the COVID19-shutdowns are coming to an end? I'd rather not using `MissionRaw` or going back to native MAVlink handling if I could avoid it :)
@julianoes I see you removed the 'feature request' tag and added the 'feature' tag to this issue. What is the difference? Is this issue getting developed now? Thanks!

> I see you removed the 'feature request' tag and added the 'feature' tag to this issue.

I was just consolidating the tags. Once we are done with the auto-generation we can consider handling yaw better in the mission plugin. Until then we can only recommend to use mission_raw which should have most features as of the next release.
@julianoes Any updates on where this might be in the queue? Thanks.
